clusters.name: your stepfather Desmond bonding, 1987
clusters.reason: Around 1987 when you began secondary school: your distance from Desmond, your pull toward your father, and the separation between your father and stepmother over a baby; your anxiety rose as you made the chess squad that autumn. These shifts sit close together in the same months.

clusters.name: your grandfather Gordon dying, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around 1989 when your grandfather came back into the family and your father's separation deepened, into the years after his death in 1991: your late nights and symptom rose, you stopped chess and debate, your mother filled in your college forms and you leaned hard on Rafe once at the conservatory; a wrist injury stopped your playing in October 1991 and you and Rafe clashed; you were alone and high, then lost and low; you dropped out and spent a bleak year at community college. Your grandfather's death sits among these shifts, and by 1994 when you raced through your degree after an exchange abroad, you found your drive again. The shifts pile up over years with only partial relief between them, each step moving you further from your footing.

clusters.name: your grandmother Winifred dying, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around 2001 when your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer and you began running out of steam for performing: your anxiety rose and functioning fell, you had a disastrous audition and were done with performing, you were on poor terms with family and friends. You left Thornbury, met Marisol in Gull Harbour, moved with her to Fenwick, and split within the year; you sank into deep depression once you were back in Thornbury that winter. You could not face your family, relied on friends, and your father spoke with Corbin who was taking you in. You requested help from your parents with therapy and returned to your therapist; your grandmother died in February 2004. The trouble moves from person to person—your functioning falling as your grandmother's symptom rose, your distance from family deepening, then shifting toward friends and helpers and back toward your parents through intermediaries.

clusters.name: your grandmother Lorna dying, 2008
clusters.reason: Around 2008 when your grandmother died and your aunt had a stroke: you went to Alder Creek for four weeks before nursing school and were too drained for your mother; she pressed to visit you, you kept the door shut, and you stopped speaking to her when you left for nursing school that August. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke with months of rehabilitation. Within this same year your grandmother and grandfather died, your aunt fell ill, and you and your mother cut off contact. The silence held roughly a year.

clusters.name: your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017 and into late 2019: your contact with your mother eased off slightly; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis; your sister Tara married and had a baby on the way; your anxiety rose as you felt you ought to be driving projects forward, and you started a sleeping pill. Around late October 2019 at Wren's mother's retirement at the lake, your partner was swamped with events and you overfunctioned laying out a plan for her; she is fused with her father and brother; you awoke from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as others rose, feeling you don't belong. Your anxiety stayed high on the long quiet drive home. Shifts pile up in your partner's family around the same months, and your sleep worsens around her family's occasions.
